analysis.scope_and_question: The study focuses on esophageal squamous papilloma (ESP), a rare benign lesion of the upper aerodigestive tract, and aims to describe a case series within a tertiary dysphagia center while evaluating the association between human papillomavirus (HPV) and chronic mucosal irritation.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A retrospective case series was conducted over a 2-year period at a tertiary center, with histopathology and DNA in-situ hybridization (ISH) for high and low-risk HPV reviewed.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: ESP is a benign entity frequently encountered incidentally during dysphagia workup, and the results support chronic irritation rather than HPV as the primary etiology.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study identifies a small sample size (five cases) and the absence of HPV detection in all specimens, suggesting a need for larger studies to confirm the etiological role of chronic irritation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Recognition of ESP is vital for otolaryngologists to ensure appropriate resection and surveillance, particularly in patients with dysphagia or heartburn.

analysis.summary_en: This case series examines esophageal squamous papilloma (ESP), a rare benign lesion, in five patients presenting with dysphagia or heartburn. All cases were incidental findings co-existing with other conditions like cricopharyngeal dysfunction. Histopathology and HPV testing showed no HPV involvement, supporting chronic irritation as the primary etiology. The study highlights the importance of ESP recognition in otolaryngology for proper management and surveillance.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) as a biomarker in head and neck cancer, specifically addressing its utility in diagnostic and surveillance settings across head and neck cancer types, including HPV-associated oropharynx cancer and Epstein-Barr virus-associated nasopharynx cancer.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A review was conducted by the American Head and Neck Society to address the current utility of ctDNA, with ongoing clinical trials reviewed to discuss its utility in monitoring treatment response and measuring minimal residual disease (MRD).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Liquid biopsy targeting viral ctDNA is a promising biomarker in the diagnostic and surveillance settings across head and neck cancer types, with ongoing clinical trials expected to elucidate its implementation for monitoring treatment response, assessing MRD, and framing treatment decisions via a precision oncology approach.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Several questions remain regarding the routine clinical use of ctDNA, including test variability and implications of inaccurate test results, necessitating optimized clinical trial designs and further research to bring ctDNA to the forefront of head and neck cancer management.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Optimized clinical trial designs and further research are necessary to bring ctDNA to the forefront of head and neck cancer management, with ongoing trials expected to help implement ctDNA for monitoring treatment response, assessing MRD, and adapting treatment via a precision oncology approach.

analysis.summary_en: This review by the American Head and Neck Society examines circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) as a promising biomarker in head and neck cancer, particularly in HPV-associated oropharynx and Epstein-Barr virus-associated nasopharynx cancers. While ctDNA shows potential for diagnostic and surveillance use, challenges such as test variability and inaccurate results remain. Ongoing clinical trials aim to clarify its utility in monitoring treatment response, assessing minimal residual disease, and guiding precision oncology approaches. Further research and optimized trial designs are needed to advance ctDNA into routine clinical practice.

analysis.scope_and_question: This study focuses on female allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant (AlloHCT) survivors aged 21-65, who are at increased risk for HPV-related malignancies due to immunosuppression. The central question explores their cervical cancer screening knowledge, behaviors, attitudes, experiences, and preferences, specifically comparing provider-collected versus self-collected methods, while identifying adherence barriers and facilitators.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A mixed-methods observational study was conducted with female AlloHCT survivors who received transplants at Oregon Health & Science University between 2012 and 2023. Participants completed demographic surveys and focus groups to explore screening adherence, perceptions, and preferences.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Cervical cancer screening preferences among AlloHCT survivors are shaped by physical and psychological treatment-related factors. All participants preferred provider-collected screening due to confidence in test accuracy and reassurance from clinician involvement. HPV self-collection may serve as a supplemental option before BMT, between annual visits, or when access barriers arise.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study identified limited access to in-network providers as a barrier to screening adherence. Psychological factors, particularly worry about recurrence or secondary cancers, strongly influenced preferences, but the study did not address broader systemic or geographic access disparities.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should explore strategies to improve access to in-network providers and address psychological barriers to screening. Practice implications include considering HPV self-collection as a supplemental option to overcome access barriers while maintaining annual provider-collected screening as the preferred method.

analysis.summary_en: This mixed-methods study examined cervical cancer screening perspectives among female AlloHCT survivors, who face elevated HPV-related malignancy risks due to immunosuppression. Participants preferred provider-collected screening for its accuracy and clinician reassurance, though psychological factors like cancer recurrence worries influenced decisions. Barriers included limited access to in-network providers, while awareness of increased risk facilitated adherence. The study suggests HPV self-collection could supplement annual screening, particularly before BMT or during access challenges. Findings highlight the need for tailored interventions addressing both physical and psychological factors to improve screening adherence in this high-risk population.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on human papillomavirus (HPV) as the etiologic agent in cervical cancer and the evolution of screening strategies toward primary HPV testing.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The article is a historical and institutional review tracing the evolution of cervical cancer screening from cytology-based approaches to HPV-based modalities, with no explicit systematic search or meta-analysis reported.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Primary HPV testing is now the preferred screening method per the American Cancer Society and anticipated endorsement by the USPSTF, with high sensitivity for detecting cervical cancer precursors.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights logistical challenges in transitioning to primary HPV testing, including triage strategies for HPV-positive cases, but does not address broader evidence gaps or conflicting findings.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The authors emphasize the need for institutional planning to manage workflow and specimen volume changes during the transition to primary HPV testing.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the historical shift from cytology-based to HPV-based cervical cancer screening, driven by the recognition of HPV as the primary etiologic agent. It details the evolution of guidelines, with primary HPV testing now preferred by the American Cancer Society and anticipated endorsement by the USPSTF. The authors present institutional experience, highlighting logistical requirements and workflow impacts during the transition, including triage strategies for HPV-positive cases. While consensus supports HPV testing's sensitivity, the review underscores practical implementation challenges without addressing broader evidence gaps.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) rely on multiple host cell factors to replicate the viral genome, yet the contribution of host long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) to viral genome maintenance and amplification in the productive life cycle remains poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study investigated the role of the lncRNA DINO in HPV DNA replication using keratinocytes, examining its effects on viral genome replication, replication foci formation, and early viral gene expression.
analysis.methods: The study measured DINO levels during keratinocyte differentiation, performed ectopic expression of DINO, and assessed its impact on HPV genome replication, replication foci formation, and early viral transcript levels, including E1^E4, E1, and E2.
analysis.main_results: DINO levels increase during keratinocyte differentiation, and ectopic expression of DINO promotes HPV genome replication and replication foci formation independently of keratinocyte differentiation signals, while also increasing select early viral transcript levels.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret DINO as a driver of HPV DNA replication, highlighting its underappreciated role in host-virus interactions, and note its context-dependent subcellular localization suggesting distinct functional roles in keratinocyte differentiation and HPV biology.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide a foundation for exploring lncRNAs as potential therapeutic targets in HPV-associated diseases, offering new insights into cellular pathways that support HPV genome replication.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study is based on in vitro experiments in keratinocytes, and while the findings are significant, further in vivo validation is needed to confirm the therapeutic potential of targeting DINO.

analysis.summary_en: This study identifies the long non-coding RNA DINO as a key regulator of human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA replication. The researchers found that DINO levels increase during keratinocyte differentiation and that its ectopic expression promotes HPV genome replication and replication foci formation independently of differentiation signals. DINO also enhances the expression of early viral transcripts, including E1^E4, E1, and E2. The study reveals that DINO exhibits context-dependent subcellular localization, suggesting distinct roles in cellular stress responses and HPV biology. These findings highlight an underappreciated role for host lncRNAs in virus-host interactions and provide new insights into potential therapeutic targets for HPV-associated diseases.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on testicular germ cell tumors (TGCTs) and penile cancer, examining molecular-based diagnosis and treatment approaches, with emphasis on biomarkers and targeted therapies.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review summarizes recent advances in TGCTs and penile cancer, highlighting emerging biomarkers and targeted therapeutic strategies, though specific databases, search dates, and study counts are not reported.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Novel biomarkers like miR-371a-3p offer higher diagnostic accuracy in TGCTs, and molecular classification based on HPV status is increasingly relevant for penile cancer prognosis and treatment selection. Actionable molecular alterations have enabled immunotherapy and anti-EGFR strategies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Conventional serum tumor markers (AFP, β-HCG, LDH) have limited sensitivity and specificity. While ctDNA shows promise for treatment monitoring, further prospective studies and standardized methodologies are needed before widespread clinical implementation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Prospective studies and standardized methodologies are required to incorporate biomarker-driven approaches into routine clinical practice, enabling more individualized management of TGCTs and penile cancer.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines molecular-based diagnosis and treatment for testicular germ cell tumors (TGCTs) and penile cancer, highlighting emerging biomarkers like miR-371a-3p and ctDNA for improved accuracy and monitoring. While conventional markers have limitations, molecular classification based on HPV status and actionable alterations are advancing personalized therapy. Despite promising data, further prospective studies are needed for clinical implementation, emphasizing the shift toward biomarker-driven precision oncology.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on therapeutic resistance in HPV-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), examining molecular mechanisms, clinical challenges, and precision strategies to address resistance to chemoradiotherapy, platinum-based chemotherapy, and EGFR-targeted therapy.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review systematically dissects the molecular architecture of treatment resistance in HPV-positive OPSCC, critically appraises contributions and limitations of patient-derived organoids, genetically engineered mouse models, and pivotal clinical trials (notably RTOG 1016).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HPV-positive OPSCC exhibits exceptional sensitivity to chemoradiotherapy with 5-year overall survival exceeding 80%, but 15%–20% of patients develop therapeutic resistance and locoregional recurrence. Core drivers of resistance include aberrant DNA damage response signaling, epigenetic reprogramming, cancer stem cell plasticity, and non-coding RNA networks.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Persistent controversies include the complex relationship between treatment de-escalation and resistance, and the lack of integrative resistance biomarkers. The review highlights unresolved mechanisms and the need for actionable vulnerabilities.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: A roadmap is proposed to bridge translational gaps and accelerate the development of precision strategies that circumvent resistance, emphasizing the need for integrative biomarkers and targeted interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines therapeutic resistance in HPV-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), which, despite high chemoradiotherapy sensitivity (5-year survival >80%), affects 15%–20% of patients, leading to poor outcomes. It systematically analyzes molecular mechanisms driving resistance to radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and EGFR-targeted therapy, including aberrant DNA damage response, epigenetic reprogramming, cancer stem cell plasticity, and non-coding RNA networks. The review critiques models like patient-derived organoids and clinical trials (e.g., RTOG 1016), addresses controversies around de-escalation and biomarker gaps, and proposes strategies to develop precision interventions to overcome resistance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-related oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is associated with improved survival compared with HPV-negative disease. However, limited evidence is available on how the risk of recurrence and cancer-related death evolves according to HPV status.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This multicentre retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent upfront surgery with neck dissection for OPSCC between 2010 and 2022.
analysis.methods: HPV status was determined by p16 immunohistochemistry. Overall survival, cancer-specific survival, disease-free survival, and disease-free specific survival were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods. Time-varying hazard rates (HR) for cancer-related death, local recurrence, regional recurrence, distant metastasis, and secondary primary tumor were estimated over a five-year period using nonparametric smoothed hazard functions, stratified by p16 status.
analysis.main_results: Among 650 patients, 284 (43.7%) had p16-positive tumours. Cancer-related mortality peaked during the second postoperative year in both groups, but occurring earlier and at markedly higher levels in p16-negative than in p16-positive patients (15 vs 18 months; annual HR: 12.7% vs 4.1%). Local and regional recurrence risks were the highest within the first two years, remained significantly higher and more prolonged in p16-negative patients than in p16-positive counterpart. The risk of second primary tumors was higher for p16-negative patients than p16-positive ones, remaining almost constant during follow-up in both groups.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The risk of recurrence and cancer-related death after surgery for OPSCC differs in magnitude and in timing according to p16 status. Hazard function analysis provides clinically relevant information beyond conventional survival estimates and may support time-adapted follow-up strategies and patient counselling in OPSCC.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may support time-adapted follow-up strategies and patient counselling in OPSCC.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a retrospective cohort study, which may introduce bias and limit the ability to establish causality. The evidence is moderate as it is based on observational data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how the risk of recurrence and cancer-related death evolves after surgery for oropharyngeal cancer (OPSCC) according to human papillomavirus (HPV) status. It is a multicentre retrospective cohort study of 650 patients with OPSCC who underwent surgery between 2010 and 2022. HPV status was determined by p16 immunohistochemistry, and hazard rates were estimated using nonparametric smoothed functions. Results show that p16-negative patients had higher cancer-related mortality and recurrence risks compared to p16-positive patients, with these risks peaking earlier in the p16-negative group. The risk of second primary tumors was also higher in p16-negative patients. The authors conclude that hazard function analysis provides clinically relevant insights beyond traditional survival estimates, potentially guiding time-adapted follow-up and patient counseling. However, the study's retrospective design limits its ability to establish causality, and the evidence is considered moderate.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health need to increase HPV vaccination uptake among males by identifying psychosocial determinants of vaccination intention using an extended Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) framework.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted between March and May 2025 in Hangzhou, China, enrolling 1,310 male undergraduate students via multi-stage stratified cluster sampling.
analysis.methods: Hierarchical linear models (three steps) and structural equation modeling (SEM) were used to quantify the contributions of sociodemographics, TPB constructs (behavior attitude, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control), HPV knowledge, and risk perception to vaccination intention.
analysis.main_results: In the final model, TPB constructs and knowledge explained 32.7% of variance in vaccination intention (F = 126.245, p < .001), with perceived behavioral control the strongest predictor (β = 0.527, p < .001), followed by behavior attitude, subjective norms, and HPV-related knowledge.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as showing that perceived behavioral control and attitudes are key levers for increasing male HPV vaccination intention, highlighting the value of an extended TPB model in this population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that policy interventions should prioritize improving vaccine accessibility and affordability while strengthening positive attitudes and social support through targeted health education to raise male HPV vaccination rates.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and reliance on self-reported intention may overestimate future uptake; the evidence is assessed as moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study in Hangzhou, China, assessed psychosocial determinants of HPV vaccination intention among 1,310 male college students using an extended Theory of Planned Behavior model. Hierarchical regression and structural equation modeling showed that perceived behavioral control, behavior attitude, subjective norms, and HPV-related knowledge together explained 32.7% of variance in vaccination intention, with perceived behavioral control the strongest predictor. The authors conclude that improving vaccine accessibility and affordability alongside targeted health education to foster positive attitudes and social support could increase male HPV vaccination uptake.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focuses on human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine availability and utilization among reproductive-age women (15–49 years) in Ikwerre Local Government Area (KELGA), Rivers State, Nigeria, examining their relationship with vaccine acceptance.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A cross-sectional descriptive survey was conducted using a structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire with 325 participants selected via simple random sampling from three primary health centres (85.5% response rate). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Chi-square tests at p < 0.05.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Vaccine availability (grand mean = 3.32) and utilization (grand mean = 3.31) were significantly associated with acceptance (X2 = 159.099 and 125.294, respectively; p = .000), confirming them as key determinants. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study identifies occasional stock shortages and low full-dose completion rates as unresolved issues, though specific causes or regional disparities in these gaps are not explored.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Health authorities should strengthen vaccine supply chain management and implement structured follow-up systems to improve dose completion and overall acceptance in similar community settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed HPV vaccine availability and utilization among reproductive-age women in KELGA, Nigeria, finding both factors significantly associated with acceptance. Despite favourable perceptions, stock shortages and incomplete dosing schedules persist. Recommendations include improving supply chain management and follow-up systems to enhance coverage.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Background Human papillomavirus-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (HPV + OPSCC) generally has favorable outcomes yet remains prone to late recurrence. Durable control likely depends on persistent tumor-specific CD8+ T cells, but their persistence and function in metastasis are poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Methods We integrated bulk RNA sequencing (n = 56) with single-cell RNA and paired T-cell receptor (TCR) sequencing of tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells (n = 4), including a longitudinal primary-lung metastasis pair obtained three years after curative therapy.
analysis.methods: HPV genotyping, HLA typing, epitope prediction, and NFAT-reporter Jurkat-luciferase assays were used to identify and functionally validate HPV16 E6/E7-specific TCRs. Repertoire tracking and single-cell/bulk transcriptomics were evaluated.
analysis.main_results: Results HPV + tumors showed higher inferred CD8+ T cell infiltration and more favorable prognosis than HPV- tumors. Single-cell analysis revealed oligoclonally expanded exhausted clusters enriched in HPV tumor-specific CD8+ T cells. Compared with the primary tumor, metastatic lesions showed reduced stem-like/TCF7-associated CD8+ T-cell populations and enrichment of HPV-specific CD8+ T cells expressing KLRB1 and ZNF683.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Conclusions High-avidity, KLRB1 + HPV-specific CD8+ T cells represent a persistent effector subset with prognostic and therapeutic relevance to HPV + OPSCC. Their persistence in metastatic lesions and association with reduced recurrence risk support further investigation of KLRB1 -associated HPV-reactive T-cell states as biomarkers and immunotherapeutic targets.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that high-avidity HPV-specific T cells may serve as biomarkers for recurrence risk and targets for immunotherapy in HPV + OPSCC, potentially improving patient outcomes through targeted interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence strength is moderate due to the small sample size (n = 4 for single-cell sequencing) and reliance on inferred data for some analyses, though the longitudinal design and functional validation strengthen the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated persistent HPV-specific activated T cells in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), focusing on HPV-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (HPV + OPSCC). The researchers integrated bulk RNA sequencing (n = 56) with single-cell RNA and TCR sequencing of tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells (n = 4), including a longitudinal primary-lung metastasis pair. They identified and validated nine patient-derived HPV16 E6/E7-specific TCRs, finding that high-avidity receptors persisted in metastatic lesions, while lower-avidity clones were lost. Metastatic lesions showed reduced stem-like T-cell populations and enrichment of HPV-specific CD8+ T cells expressing KLRB1 and ZNF683, indicating a tissue-adapted state. The study concludes that high-avidity, KLRB1 + HPV-specific CD8+ T cells are a persistent effector subset with prognostic and therapeutic relevance, supporting their investigation as biomarkers and immunotherapeutic targets.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Women with autoimmune inflammatory rheumatic diseases (AIIRDs) are more vulnerable to human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and HPV-related cervical cancers, however, the HPV screening and vaccination rate was low.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a real-world survey to evaluate the awareness and status of HPV vaccination in Chinese AIIRDs patients. Female patients with AIIRDs aged ≥ 9 years were enrolled between 1 April 2024 and 31 Aug 2024.
analysis.methods: Eligible participants completed a predefined 41-item questionnaire, which was distributed via social media invitations and in-person recruitment at outpatient clinics. We evaluated the demographics, rheumatic disease history, awareness of HPV infection and vaccination, HPV testing and vaccination status and willingness to receive HPV vaccine.
analysis.main_results: A total of 562 participants with a median age of 34.9 (IQR 29.7–42.6) years completed the questionnaires. The awareness rates of HPV infection and vaccination were 82.0% and 85.9%, respectively. However, only 69.2% participants recognized the increased risk of cervical cancer associated with HPV, and just 52.3% had undergone cervical cancer screening in the past 5 years. Although 72.2% expressed willingness to receive the HPV vaccine, the actual vaccination rate was only 23.0%. Among the respondents, there were 334 SLE patients and 98 RA patients. Compared to RA patients, SLE patients were younger, had higher awareness of HPV vaccination, but a lower vaccination rate.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Patients with AIIRDs, SLE in particular, demonstrate high awareness of HPV infection and vaccination, as well as strong willingness to receive HPV vaccine. However, cervical cancer screening and actual HPV vaccination rates remain low.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need to address modifiable barriers to HPV vaccination in Chinese AIIRDs patients, particularly SLE patients, to improve vaccination coverage and reduce the risk of HPV-related cervical cancer.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data, which may introduce recall bias. The evidence strength is moderate due to the large sample size but the lack of randomization and potential selection bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated HPV vaccination awareness and status in Chinese women with autoimmune inflammatory rheumatic diseases (AIIRDs). A real-world survey of 562 participants revealed high awareness of HPV infection (82.0%) and vaccination (85.9%), with strong willingness to receive the vaccine (72.2%). However, actual vaccination rates were low (23.0%), and only 52.3% had undergone cervical cancer screening in the past 5 years. SLE patients showed higher awareness but lower vaccination rates compared to RA patients. The findings underscore the need to address barriers to HPV vaccination in this high-risk population to reduce HPV-related cancer risks.

analysis.scope_and_question: This scoping review focuses on the interconnections between infectious diseases (IDs) and non-communicable diseases (NCDs), exploring integrated strategies for their prevention and management. The central question is how to address the bidirectional links between these disease categories through shared mechanisms, overlapping risk factors, and pathways.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A scoping review was conducted by systematically searching PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus for English-language systematic reviews and meta-analyses published between January 1, 2000, and April 20, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened eligible studies and extracted effect estimates for associations between IDs and NCDs.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review identified 41 meta-analyses or systematic reviews showing associations between pathogen infections and specific cancers, such as hepatitis B and C viruses with liver cancer, human papillomavirus with cervical cancer, and Helicobacter pylori with gastric cancer. IDs were also linked to increased NCD burdens, and NCDs like diabetes or cardiovascular disease were associated with higher risks of severe outcomes following IDs such as tuberculosis, influenza, or COVID-19.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that research, health policy, and prevention practices still largely address IDs and NCDs in separate frameworks, despite evidence of their interconnections. There is a need for more integrated approaches to address the shared mechanisms and overlapping risk factors between these disease categories.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: At the public health level, the review calls for health policies and financing mechanisms to move beyond disease-specific silos towards systemic frameworks that support integrated prevention and control, coordinated management, and cross-sectoral action. This includes combining prevention, early detection, treatment, and long-term management strategies for both IDs and NCDs.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review examines the bidirectional links between infectious diseases (IDs) and non-communicable diseases (NCDs), highlighting their interconnections through shared mechanisms and overlapping risk factors. The review analyzed 41 meta-analyses and systematic reviews, finding associations between pathogens like HPV and specific cancers, and between NCDs like diabetes and severe outcomes from IDs. The evidence underscores the need for integrated strategies that combine prevention, early detection, treatment, and long-term management. Public health policies are urged to move beyond disease-specific silos to support coordinated, cross-sectoral action for addressing both IDs and NCDs simultaneously.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on small cell carcinoma of the cervix (SCCC), a rare and aggressive subtype of cervical cancer, examining its molecular mechanisms, clinical management, and therapeutic targets. The central question revolves around understanding the dual pathogenic mechanisms involving high-risk human papillomavirus (hr-HPV) and HPV-independent oncogenic pathways.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on current clinical understanding and molecular mechanisms of SCCC, synthesizing evidence from existing literature. It does not specify databases, search dates, or study counts but emphasizes a closed-loop model integrating basic research and clinical application.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: SCCC is driven by hr-HPV infection (particularly HPV18) and involves cooperative regulation at multiple molecular levels, including HPV genome integration, gene mutations, and aberrant signaling pathways. A dual pathogenic mechanism exists, combining HPV-dependent and HPV-independent pathways mediated by TP53 and RB1 mutations.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the complexity of SCCC pathogenesis, including tumor heterogeneity, therapeutic resistance, and metastasis, but does not explicitly address conflicting findings or specific evidence gaps. The role of HPV-independent pathways and their interaction with HPV-driven mechanisms remains an area needing further elucidation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes potential novel therapeutic targets for SCCC and emphasizes the need for dynamic iteration between basic research and clinical practice. It suggests that basic research should be oriented toward real clinical problems, with reciprocal feedback from clinical practice to drive collaborative breakthroughs.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines small cell carcinoma of the cervix (SCCC), a rare and aggressive cervical cancer subtype, focusing on its molecular mechanisms and clinical management. It highlights the dual pathogenic drivers: high-risk human papillomavirus (hr-HPV, particularly HPV18) and HPV-independent oncogenic pathways involving TP53 and RB1 mutations. The review proposes a closed-loop model integrating basic research and clinical application, emphasizing reciprocal feedback to address tumor heterogeneity, therapeutic resistance, and metastasis. It identifies potential novel therapeutic targets and underscores the need for collaborative breakthroughs between research and practice.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Warts are a common pediatric condition caused by human papillomavirus, and immunotherapy is a well-studied treatment for warts.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We report a case of warts in a 12-year-old boy who achieved complete resolution following two sessions of intralesional Candida antigen administered using a needle-free jet injection device.
analysis.methods: The treatment involved pain-free, needleless intralesional Candida antigen administered using a needle-free jet injection device.
analysis.main_results: The patient achieved complete resolution of warts following two sessions of treatment.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This approach represents a less painful alternative for administration of intralesional immunotherapy, particularly useful in pediatric or needle-phobic patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This method offers a more comfortable option for wart treatment, potentially improving adherence in pediatric populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on a single case report, limiting generalizability and strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study reports a case of wart treatment in a 12-year-old boy using a needle-free jet injection device to administer intralesional Candida antigen. The patient achieved complete resolution after two painless sessions, demonstrating a less painful alternative to traditional needle-based immunotherapy. This method is particularly beneficial for pediatric patients or those with needle phobia, offering a more comfortable treatment option. However, the evidence is limited to a single case report, which restricts its generalizability and strength.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Adolescent vaccination rates for meningococcal, human papillomavirus (HPV), and tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis remain suboptimal despite public health recommendations, creating a need for targeted interventions to improve coverage and equity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This quality-improvement study was conducted in an adolescent medicine practice using a bundled intervention approach after a current-state analysis to identify gaps in vaccination documentation and administration.
analysis.methods: The team applied the Model for Improvement framework and implemented a multi-component intervention including obtaining missing vaccination records, provider notifications, electronic medical record alerts for due vaccinations, patient education, and nurse-administered numbing spray to address needle-related hesitancy.
analysis.main_results: Statistical process control charts demonstrated an increase in complete vaccination records from 88% to 95% and a mean shift in combined meningococcal, HPV, and Tdap completion from 70% to 76%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The bundled intervention was associated with higher rates of vaccine documentation and administration, with improvements observed across all race and payer subgroups, suggesting that system-level changes can enhance HPV vaccination coverage and reduce disparities.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the implementation of system-level interventions such as provider alerts, patient education, and procedural accommodations to improve HPV vaccination rates and advance health equity in adolescent care.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s reliance on a single-center design and lack of randomization limits causal inference, though the observed improvements across diverse subgroups strengthen the evidence base for practice-level interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This quality-improvement study in an adolescent medicine practice aimed to increase vaccination completion rates for meningococcal, HPV, and Tdap vaccines while addressing equity gaps. Using the Model for Improvement, the team implemented a bundled intervention that included provider notifications, electronic alerts, patient education, and procedural accommodations such as numbing spray. Statistical process control charts showed significant improvements, with complete vaccination records rising from 88% to 95% and combined completion rates increasing from 70% to 76%. Improvements were observed across all racial and payer subgroups, indicating that system-level changes can enhance HPV vaccination coverage and reduce disparities. While the single-center design and absence of randomization limit causal conclusions, the findings support practice-level interventions to improve HPV vaccination rates and advance health equity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of regulating conformational changes in perfectly matched DNA systems, which is critical for developing advanced molecular devices.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research involved the design and assembly of a two-dimensional DNA triangle using only two short DNA strands, with the focus on its structural transformation in response to RNA sequences.
analysis.methods: The methods included the use of toehold-mediated strand displacement to trigger structural changes, and the transformation pathways were validated through cryogenic-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and mass spectrometry (MS) analyses.
analysis.main_results: Strand displacement induced by the corresponding RNA sequence altered the assembly pathway of the DNA triangle, resulting in the formation of a three-dimensional RNA-DNA hybrid quadrilateral without the need for a toehold.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that RNA strand displacement provides a new strategy for constructing dynamic DNA nanostructures, which could be useful in molecular diagnostics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results may inform the development of more efficient and specific signal reporting systems for detecting HPV in clinical settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level evidence, and the experimental design does not provide detailed validation of the system's performance in real-world clinical scenarios.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the use of RNA strand displacement to induce structural transformation in DNA nanostructures, offering a novel approach for molecular diagnostics. The research demonstrates that RNA can trigger the formation of a three-dimensional hybrid structure without requiring a toehold, which is a significant advancement in the field. The findings highlight the potential of this method for detecting HPV in clinical samples, although the evidence is limited to abstract-level descriptions. The study's design and validation methods are supported by cryogenic-electron microscopy and mass spectrometry analyses, which confirm the structural changes. While the results are promising, the lack of detailed clinical data and the focus on abstract-level reporting suggest that further research is needed to assess the practical applications of this technology. The implications of this work could contribute to the development of more sensitive and specific diagnostic tools for HPV-related diseases.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the clinicopathological characteristics, immunohistochemical profiles and HPV status of "synchronous" endocervical and ovarian adenocarcinoma.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis of 21 cases of "synchronous" endocervical and ovarian adenocarcinoma was conducted.
analysis.methods: HE staining was used for morphological observation, IHC staining was performed to detect expression of p16, Mucin 6, Claudin18.2, NapsinA, and P504S, and testing for human papillomavirus (HPV) infection was carried out using the RNAscope method.
analysis.main_results: Among the 21 cervical cancer cases, eight exhibited pseudostratified nuclear arrangement with prominent apical mitotic figures and apoptotic bodies, 11 had cells with clear cytoplasm and distinct cell borders, while the remaining two displayed hobnail cells. IHC analysis revealed that all eight cases of both cervical and ovarian adenocarcinoma exhibited diffuse and strong positivity for p16, 11 cases co-expressed Claudin18.2 and Mucin 6, and two cases were positive for both NapsinA and P504S. RNAscope testing results were positive for all eight endocervical and ovarian adenocarcinoma cases.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the diagnosis of ovarian metastasis from EAC requires careful integration of morphological features with other clinicopathological characteristics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that p16, Claudin18.2 and Mucin 6 are useful markers for diagnosis, with HPV RNAscope testing recommended when necessary.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and the lack of longitudinal data, but the evidence is strong due to the detailed clinicopathological analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a retrospective analysis of 21 cases of "synchronous" endocervical and ovarian adenocarcinoma to investigate their clinicopathological characteristics, immunohistochemical profiles, and HPV status. Morphological features were observed using HE staining, while IHC staining was used to detect p16, Mucin 6, Claudin18.2, NapsinA, and P504S. HPV infection was tested using RNAscope. The results showed that eight cases exhibited pseudostratified nuclear arrangement with prominent apical mitotic figures and apoptotic bodies, while 11 had cells with clear cytoplasm and distinct cell borders. IHC analysis revealed that all eight cases of both cervical and ovarian adenocarcinoma exhibited diffuse and strong positivity for p16, 11 cases co-expressed Claudin18.2 and Mucin 6, and two cases were positive for both NapsinA and P504S. RNAscope testing was positive for all eight cases. The authors concluded that the diagnosis of ovarian metastasis from endocervical adenocarcinoma requires careful integration of morphological features with other clinicopathological characteristics. They also highlighted the utility of p16, Claudin18.2, and Mucin 6 as diagnostic markers, with HPV RNAscope testing recommended when necessary. The study is limited by its retrospective design but provides strong evidence based on detailed clinicopathological analysis.

analysis.time: Published on 2026-07-29. Event dates not specified in the evidence.
analysis.location_and_population: Singapore (study 1) and outpatient opioid treatment program patients in the United States (study 2). Study 1: 640 women aged 30-69. Study 2: 194 patients, with 174 eligible (89%), 19 recently screened, and 1 ineligible.
analysis.event: Two studies examined women's response to HPV self-sampling testing. Both studies found that when offered, women prefer self-collection over clinician testing. The Singapore study was published in the Annals of Family Medicine, and the U.S. study was published in JAMA Network Open.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Singapore study: 56.5% of women in the intervention group underwent HPV screening compared to 42.8% in the usual-care group. High-risk HPV detection was 3.1% in the intervention group versus 0.3% in the usual-care group. study: 158 (90.8%) of eligible patients agreed to self-collection testing; 30 tested positive for HPV (7 for HPV-16/18, 23 for other high-risk strains).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Singapore study: Offering self-sampling alongside clinician sampling significantly increased screening uptake and high-risk HPV detection. study: Self-collection testing was feasible and acceptable with high patient eligibility and uptake. Follow-up care was provided for 16 of the 30 patients with positive tests. The studies suggest self-collection could improve screening rates in underserved populations.

analysis.brief_en: Two recent studies highlight women's strong preference for self-collection HPV testing when offered. In Singapore, a study of 640 women found that providing self-sampling options increased screening uptake to 56.5% compared to 42.8% in the usual-care group, with a higher detection rate of high-risk HPV strains (3.1% vs. 0.3%). Similarly, a U.S. study involving 194 patients in an opioid treatment program found that 90.8% of eligible participants agreed to self-collection testing, with 30 testing positive for HPV. Both studies, published in the Annals of Family Medicine and JAMA Network Open respectively, conclude that self-collection testing is feasible, acceptable, and effective at expanding screening rates in underserved populations, potentially reducing healthcare disparities and cervical cancer mortality.

analysis.time: Publication date: July 27, 2026. Event period: Not explicitly stated, but the trial was conducted in Singapore with results reported in 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: Target population: Women aged 30 to 69 due for cervical cancer screening. Study sample: 650 women randomly assigned to intervention (325) or usual care (325) arms.
analysis.event: A pragmatic randomized controlled trial in Singapore tested whether offering self-collected HPV samples alongside clinician-collected specimens would improve cervical cancer screening participation and HPV detection rates. The intervention group was offered clinician sampling first, with self-sampling if declined, while the usual-care group received clinician sampling only.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: HPV detection rates: 3.1% in intervention arm vs. 0.3% in usual-care arm. Screening uptake: 56.6% in intervention arm vs. 42.8% in usual-care arm. Seven of ten high-risk HPV cases were among previously unscreened women, with five detected via self-sampling. No explicit risk level stated, but improved detection suggests reduced risk of missed cervical cancer opportunities.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The trial supports patient-centered screening strategies with self-sampling as an accessible alternative. Equity concerns noted: women with lower education were less likely to choose self-sampling. The study is a completed randomized controlled trial with clear results, but limitations include potential generalizability beyond Singapore and the need for equity-sensitive design improvements.

analysis.brief_en: A pragmatic randomized controlled trial in Singapore demonstrated that offering self-collected HPV samples alongside clinician-collected specimens significantly improved cervical cancer screening rates and HPV detection. Among 650 women aged 30-69, the intervention group achieved 56.6% screening uptake (vs. 42.8% in usual care) and 3.1% HPV detection (vs. 0.3%). Notably, seven of ten high-risk HPV cases were in previously unscreened women, with five detected via self-sampling. This suggests self-sampling lowers barriers without compromising high-risk HPV identification, though equity concerns persist for women with lower education. The findings support patient-centered strategies to improve both first-time and ongoing screening participation.

analysis.brief_en: Cervical cancer is the most common cancer among women in Thailand, with over 6,000 new cases and 2,600 deaths annually. Ramkhamhaeng Hospital provides PCR-based HPV testing, combining sample collection during pelvic exams with results within seven days. Early intervention through regular screening can prevent progression, as precancerous lesions take years to develop. Women aged 30+ are advised to undergo combined Pap smear and HPV testing every three years if normal, or more frequently if inconclusive. Prevention remains key, with early detection being the most effective strategy.

analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Court directed the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Indian Council of Medical Research, and Central Drugs Standard Control Organization to file detailed replies; vaccination continues while legal challenge is pending; safety and consent procedures remain under examination.

analysis.brief_en: The Delhi High Court has allowed India’s HPV vaccination campaign to proceed after declining an interim stay, citing no immediate harm to justify suspension. The court, however, emphasized the need for further examination of informed consent, safety evidence, and monitoring protocols. The nationwide campaign, targeting adolescent girls aged 14, has already administered over 55 lakh doses, with approximately 120 minor adverse events reported. The petitioners, including a gynecologist and health entrepreneur, raised concerns about bodily autonomy, informed consent, and potential pressure on health workers. The government defended the vaccine’s global safety record, citing use in 160 countries. The court has sought detailed responses from health authorities while the vaccination drive continues.

analysis.time: Publication date: 28 July 2026. Event date: 29 July 2026 (announcement date). Analysis period: 42 months (test data collection).
analysis.location_and_population: Global healthcare institutions (through the Global Million Clinical Study). Affected population: Individuals undergoing HPV and STI testing, with focus on reproductive tract infections and cervical cancer risk assessment.
analysis.event: Seegene announced a comprehensive syndromic PCR-based testing approach for reproductive tract infections (RTIs), detecting both STIs and HPV simultaneously. This follows the launch of the Global Million Clinical Study on 8 July 2026. The announcement is based on analysis of 60,000 test results and is presented as scientific evidence supporting a new global standard for PCR testing.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Analysis of 60,000 test results showed STI pathogens were detected in 82% of HPV-positive cases, HPV in 46% of STI-positive cases, and co-detection in 71% of positive cases. The findings support the potential application of concurrent STI testing with HPV screening for identifying asymptomatic STIs, assessing co-infections, and supporting reproductive health evaluations. No explicit risk level is stated.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Seegene is validating the clinical utility of comprehensive HPV & STI testing through the Global Million Clinical Study, using STAgoraTM for real-world data accumulation and statistical evaluation. The initiative aims to establish scientific evidence for new global PCR testing standards. The analysis is based on internal company data and represents preliminary findings that require further validation through the ongoing study.

Based on analysis of 60,000 test results collected over 42 months, the company found that STI pathogens were present in 82% of HPV-positive cases, HPV in 46% of STI-positive cases, and co-detection in 71% of positive cases. These findings support the potential value of comprehensive testing for cervical cancer risk assessment and reproductive health diagnostics. The announcement follows Seegene's launch of the Global Million Clinical Study on July 8, 2026, which aims to generate scientific evidence for a new global standard of PCR testing by accumulating real-world clinical data from healthcare institutions worldwide.

analysis.location_and_population: Kenya; Focus on girls aged 9-14 as the primary target group for HPV vaccination, with emphasis on reaching communities facing barriers to healthcare access.

analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Kenya reports approximately 5,845 new cervical cancer cases and 3,591 deaths annually (GLOBOCAN 2022 data); Globally, 660,000 women were diagnosed with cervical cancer in 2022, with 350,000 deaths. The burden is heaviest in low- and middle-income countries.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Kenya introduced HPV vaccination in 2019, initially targeting 10-year-old girls, and transitioned to a single-dose schedule in November 2025 per WHO recommendations. Screening remains a complementary strategy for women aged 25-49, with HPV testing recommended for those over 30 where available. No current outbreak or investigation status is reported.

analysis.brief_en: Kenya faces a significant burden of cervical cancer, with approximately 5,845 new cases and 3,591 deaths annually. To address this, the country has implemented HPV vaccination as a key preventive measure, targeting girls aged 9-14 before potential exposure to the virus. In November 2025, Kenya transitioned from a two-dose to a single-dose HPV vaccination schedule, aligning with WHO recommendations to improve accessibility and reduce barriers in communities. While vaccination is crucial, it is not a replacement for cervical cancer screening, which remains essential for early detection in women aged 25-49. This integrated approach aims to reduce cervical cancer incidence and mortality by combining vaccination with regular screening and early treatment of precancerous lesions.

analysis.brief_en: A new oral therapy, SHetA2, shows promise in stopping persistent HPV infections from progressing to cervical cancer by targeting cancer-causing proteins. Developed by the University of Oklahoma and ICMR-NICPR, the therapy disrupts the interaction between the HPV-E7 protein and human cells, allowing the body's natural defenses to destroy the virus. While it cannot prevent HPV infection, it may benefit women with precancerous lesions or early-stage cervical cancer. In India, where cervical cancer is the second most common cancer among women, causing over 79,000 new cases and 36,000 deaths in 2024, this treatment could fill a critical gap. Larger clinical trials are underway, with potential availability in up to five years. The therapy is expected to be affordable and administered orally, reducing the need for hospital visits. Doctors emphasize that it will complement, not replace, HPV vaccination and screening programs.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the roles of cellular polymerases, including replicative and translesion synthesis (TLS) polymerases, in the life cycle of high-risk human papillomaviruses (HPVs), particularly HPV16, HPV18, HPV31, HPV33, HPV45, HPV52, and HPV58, which are causally linked to cervical, anogenital, and head and neck cancers. The central question focuses on identifying the full complement of polymerases deployed during distinct stages of the HPV life cycle and their contributions to viral replication, genomic instability, and oncogenesis.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative minireview that synthesizes existing evidence on the involvement of cellular polymerases in HPV genome replication and oncogenesis. It does not report a systematic search, eligibility criteria, included-study count, or meta-analytic methods. The review highlights gaps in understanding the complete polymerase milieu utilized by HPV across its life cycle.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: There is consensus that high-risk HPVs exploit host DNA damage tolerance pathways, including specific cellular polymerases, to support productive replication, which contributes to genomic instability and oncogenesis. However, the full complement of polymerases involved in HPV genome replication remains poorly defined, and the specific roles of replicative versus TLS polymerases at distinct life cycle stages are not fully elucidated.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies a critical gap in knowledge regarding the complete set of polymerases deployed by HPV during its life cycle, particularly the relative contributions of replicative and TLS polymerases. The lack of definitive evidence on which polymerases are essential at each stage and their roles in driving mutagenic potential and cancer progression remains unresolved.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for new experimental tools and approaches to assess the importance of specific polymerases in HPV replication, life cycle progression, and oncogenic potential. Priorities include identifying polymerase targets for antiviral strategies, understanding polymerase-mediated mutagenic processes, and developing tools to dissect polymerase contributions to HPV-associated cancers.

analysis.summary_en: This minireview explores how high-risk human papillomaviruses (HPVs), including HPV16, HPV18, and others, exploit host cellular polymerases—both replicative and translesion synthesis (TLS) enzymes—to support their life cycle and drive oncogenesis. While it is established that HPV leverages host DNA damage tolerance pathways to enable productive replication and genomic instability, the full complement of polymerases involved remains undefined. The review highlights unresolved questions about the specific roles of different polymerases at distinct life cycle stages and their contributions to mutagenic potential and cancer development. It calls for the development of new tools to dissect these mechanisms and identify potential antiviral targets.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study examines psychosocial determinants of mothers’ intentions to vaccinate their adolescent sons against human papillomavirus (HPV) in Japan, where HPV vaccination for males is not routine, focusing on factors distinguishing accepting, undecided, and refusing intention groups.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A web-based cross-sectional survey targeted mothers with boys aged 11–16 years in Japan, classifying participants into accepting, undecided, and refusing intention groups and using binary logistic regression to compare accepting versus undecided and accepting versus refusing groups.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Normative beliefs showed the strongest association with vaccination intention, with odds ratios of 12.63 (95% CI 6.03–26.47) for accepting versus undecided and 26.72 (95% CI 9.69–73.74) for accepting versus refusing groups. Associations were generally stronger in comparisons between accepting and refusing groups than between accepting and undecided groups.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The undecided group reported greater perceived logistical hassle, and the refusing group was less likely to have completed children’s routine childhood vaccinations or eldest son’s influenza vaccination, indicating potential behavioral and attitudinal gaps in vaccine uptake.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Tailored interventions are needed, including enhancing subjective norms and perceived prevention value, providing logistical support for undecided mothers, and implementing multi-channel trust-building communication strategies for refusing mothers to prioritize boys’ HPV vaccination in Japan.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates psychosocial factors influencing mothers’ intentions to vaccinate their adolescent sons against HPV in Japan, where male HPV vaccination is not routine. Using a cross-sectional survey of mothers with boys aged 11–16 years, the research classified participants into accepting, undecided, and refusing intention groups and applied binary logistic regression to compare groups. Normative beliefs emerged as the strongest correlate of vaccination intention, with markedly higher odds ratios when comparing accepting versus refusing groups than accepting versus undecided groups. The undecided group reported greater perceived logistical hassle, while the refusing group showed lower uptake of routine childhood and influenza vaccinations. The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions, including strengthening subjective norms, improving perceived prevention value, addressing logistical barriers for undecided mothers, and employing multi-channel trust-building strategies for refusing mothers to enhance HPV vaccination uptake among boys in Japan.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cutaneous verrucae (warts) are benign epidermal proliferations caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. The host immune response particularly T helper 17 (Th17) related cytokines such as interleukin-17A (IL-17A) and interleukin-23 (IL-23) plays a critical role in the regulation of viral control and inflammatory responses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In this case-control study, 49 patients with palmoplantar or anogenital verrucae and 41 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were included.
analysis.methods: Serum IL-17A and IL-23 levels were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Continuous variables were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test, and categorical variables using the chi-square test. Correlations between variables were assessed using Spearman correlation analysis.
analysis.main_results: The median serum IL-23 level was 11.8 pg/mL (interquartile range, IQR: 7.8-21.3) in patients with cutaneous verrucae and 8.8 pg/mL (IQR: 7.2-12.0) in controls, with a statistically significant difference (p = 0.018). The median serum IL-17A level was 16.6 pg/mL (IQR: 8.7-37.9) in patients and 16.4 pg/mL (IQR: 10.9-24.5) in controls, with no significant difference between the groups (p = 0.755). A strong positive correlation was observed between IL-17A and IL-23 levels in patients (rs = 0.880, p < 0.001). No significant associations were found between cytokine levels and age, sex, number of lesions, disease duration, or localization.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Elevated IL-23 levels and its strong positive correlation with IL-17A suggest that the IL-23/IL-17Axis may play a role in immune activation associated with HPV-related cutaneous verrucae.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: IL-23 may represent a potential indicator of immune activation associated with cutaneous verrucae; however, its standalone diagnostic utility appears limited.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its relatively small sample size and the lack of tissue-level analyses.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the systemic levels of IL-17A and IL-23 in patients with cutaneous verrucae caused by HPV infection and compares them to healthy controls. The research highlights the potential role of the IL-23/IL-17 axis in immune activation associated with HPV-related warts, as evidenced by elevated IL-23 levels and a strong positive correlation with IL-17A. However, the study notes that these cytokine levels are not significantly associated with demographic or clinical factors such as age, sex, or lesion localization. The findings suggest that IL-23 may serve as a potential indicator of immune activation but lack standalone diagnostic utility. The study is limited by its small sample size and absence of tissue-level analyses, which could provide more detailed insights into cytokine dynamics in HPV infection.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination in rural communities, focusing on multilevel interventions to increase uptake in Georgia. The central question addresses the effectiveness of minigrant-funded, multilevel strategies in improving HPV vaccination rates among rural populations.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review describes a concurrent, mixed-methods evaluation using RE-AIM and CFIR frameworks. Four health departments received funding, a toolkit, and technical assistance for 1 year. Data sources included program documents, staff interviews and surveys, immunization databases, and caregiver or young adult surveys.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Multilevel intervention strategies, including patient education, incentives, provider training, and patient reminders, increased HPV vaccination rates in rural settings. Total HPV vaccination rates rose by 26.7% from 2023 to early 2024, with initiation rates increasing by 51.8%. Sites reported high feasibility (mean 4.4), acceptability (mean 4.4), and appropriateness (mean 4.2) of the program.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Barriers to implementation included limited resources, communication challenges, structural issues (e.g., technology and electronic health records), and local attitudes. Sustainability capacity was moderate (mean 4.2), with highest scores for evaluation, effectiveness, and workflow integration, indicating potential long-term challenges.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future efforts should prioritize addressing resource limitations and structural barriers to enhance program sustainability. Research should focus on optimizing multilevel strategies and evaluating their long-term impact on vaccination rates in rural populations.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates a minigrant program supporting multilevel interventions to promote HPV vaccination in rural Georgia. Using RE-AIM and CFIR frameworks, four health departments implemented strategies such as patient education, incentives, provider training, and reminders over one year. Results showed a 26.7% increase in total HPV vaccination rates and a 51.8% rise in initiation rates from 2023 to early 2024. Sites reported high feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness of the program, with strong sustainability capacity in evaluation and workflow integration. However, barriers like limited resources, communication issues, and structural challenges persisted. The findings underscore the potential of multilevel interventions to boost HPV vaccination in rural settings while highlighting the need for sustained support and resource allocation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer (CC) is the fourth leading cause of cancer death in women worldwide. High-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) testing is highly sensitive but lacks specificity for identifying women at risk of progression.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Cervical scrape samples from HR-HPV-positive women were histologically classified as low-grade (≤CIN1) or high-grade (CIN2/3). Total RNA was extracted and small RNA sequencing performed to identify differentially expressed miRNAs.
analysis.methods: Bioinformatic analyses included clustering, ROC curves, logistic regression, and functional enrichment.
analysis.main_results: Nineteen dysregulated miRNAs distinguished low- from high-grade lesions, six linked to viral and cancer pathways. Three (hsa-miR-501-3p, hsa-miR-1271-5p, hsa-miR-9-5p) were validated by RT-qPCR and showed strong discriminatory capacity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This pioneering study in Colombia using cervical scrapes demonstrates that miRNAs are potential biomarkers for high-grade cervical lesions and that this clinically relevant, minimally invasive sample routinely collected in screening supports their use.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The validated signature achieved high sensitivity and specificity for detecting high-grade lesions. This could inform the development of more accurate diagnostic tools for cervical cancer screening.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations. The study demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy and strong discriminatory capacity, suggesting moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify microRNAs as potential biomarkers for triage of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia in HR-HPV-positive women. Cervical scrape samples were collected and classified histologically as low-grade (≤CIN1) or high-grade (CIN2/3). Total RNA was extracted, and small RNA sequencing was performed to identify differentially expressed miRNAs. Bioinformatic analyses included clustering, ROC curves, logistic regression, and functional enrichment. Nineteen dysregulated miRNAs were found to distinguish low- from high-grade lesions, with six linked to viral and cancer pathways. Three miRNAs (hsa-miR-501-3p, hsa-miR-1271-5p, hsa-miR-9-5p) were validated by RT-qPCR and showed strong discriminatory capacity. The validated signature achieved high sensitivity and specificity for detecting high-grade lesions. The study concludes that miRNAs are potential biomarkers for high-grade cervical lesions and that cervical scrape samples, routinely collected in screening, support their use. The evidence strength is moderate, as the study does not report limitations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Invasive cervical cancer (ICC) is a critical endpoint for evaluating cervical cancer screening programs, and distinguishing cancers detected within versus outside organized screening is essential to assess program impact during transitions such as the adoption of human papillomavirus (HPV)-based primary screening.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective population-based study was conducted in Portugal’s Central Region from 2014 to 2023, linking organized cervical cancer screening database records with hospital morbidity data to classify ICC cases as screen-detected or non-screen-detected.
analysis.methods: Deterministic linkage between screening and hospital records was performed to classify ICC cases, and incidence rates were calculated using population denominators. Poisson regression models with log link and log-transformed population offsets estimated incidence rate ratios (IRR) comparing cytology-based (2014–2019) and HPV-based (2020–2023) screening periods, adjusting for temporal trends.
analysis.main_results: A total of 654 ICC cases were included, with screening participation remaining broadly stable over time. The HPV-based screening period was associated with a significantly higher rate of screen-detected ICC (IRR = 1.94; 95% CI 1.11–3.40) compared with the cytology period, while ICC incidence outside the organized screening program did not differ significantly between periods (IRR = 0.94; 95% CI 0.65–1.35).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that the transition to HPV-based primary screening shifted ICC detection toward the organized screening program without increasing incidence among women diagnosed outside it, supporting a detection shift within the screening pathway rather than changes in underlying disease occurrence.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that HPV-based primary screening may improve early detection of ICC within organized programs, highlighting the importance of integrating screening, hospital, and cancer registry data for robust policy evaluation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the early phase of HPV-based screening implementation and potential external factors influencing diagnostic access, which may limit generalizability and causal inference.

analysis.summary_en: This population-based study in Portugal assessed the impact of transitioning from cytology-based to HPV-based primary cervical cancer screening on invasive cervical cancer (ICC) detection. Using deterministic linkage between screening and hospital records from 2014 to 2023, the authors classified ICC cases as screen-detected or non-screen-detected and calculated incidence rates. Poisson regression models showed that the HPV-based screening period was associated with a significantly higher rate of screen-detected ICC (IRR 1.94, 95% CI 1.11–3.40) compared to the cytology period, while ICC incidence outside the organized screening program remained unchanged (IRR 0.94, 95% CI 0.65–1.35). The findings indicate a shift in detection toward the organized screening pathway without evidence of increased underlying disease occurrence. However, the early implementation phase and potential external diagnostic access factors warrant cautious interpretation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the evolving management of cervical squamous cell carcinoma with unknown primary (SCCUP), particularly the debated role of bilateral tonsillectomy in identifying the primary site in HPV-negative patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective observational study enrolled 21 patients with SCCUP who underwent bilateral tonsillectomy to identify a potential primary site, with a median age of 59 years (range 39–74 years).
analysis.methods: The study performed bilateral tonsillectomy in 21 patients with SCCUP to attempt identification of a primary lesion, with adjuvant treatments including concurrent chemoradiation in 15 patients and radiotherapy in 2 patients.
analysis.main_results: Only 1 of 20 patients (p16 positive) revealed a primary in the tonsil, while 2 patients were p16 positive. The 2-year overall and disease-free survival rates were 81.5% (52.6%–93.7%) and 70.1% (42.1%–86.4%), respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that the prevalence of HPV in SCCUP is very low in India and that the role of bilateral tonsillectomy to identify primary lesions in p16-negative patients is questionable.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest limited utility of bilateral tonsillectomy for identifying primary sites in HPV-negative SCCUP, which may inform surgical decision-making and reduce unnecessary interventions in this population.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The small sample size (n=21), short median follow-up (17.6 months), and lack of mucosal recurrence data limit the strength of evidence, warranting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective observational study evaluated the role of bilateral tonsillectomy in identifying primary lesions among 21 patients with cervical squamous cell carcinoma of unknown primary (SCCUP). Only one p16-positive patient had a primary lesion identified in the tonsil, while two patients were p16 positive, indicating a low HPV prevalence in this cohort. The 2-year overall and disease-free survival rates were 81.5% and 70.1%, respectively. The authors conclude that bilateral tonsillectomy has questionable utility for identifying primary lesions in p16-negative SCCUP, particularly in settings with low HPV prevalence. However, the small sample size and short follow-up period limit the generalizability and strength of these findings.
